In the 1950s, Central American commercial banana growers faced the death of their most profitable crop, the Gros Michel banana, known as Big Mike. Now it's happening again to Big Mike's successor, the Cavendish. With its easy-to-grow, thick-skinned, and sweet-tasting fruit, the Gros Michel banana plant dominated the plantations of Central America. United Fruit, the main grower and exporter in South America at the time, mass-produced its bananas in the most efficient way possible: it cloned shoots from the stems of plants instead of growing plants from seeds, and cultivated them in densely packed fields.

Spider venom is found in many species and serves as a defense mechanism. Only 25 out of the known spider species produce venom capable of harming humans. Although rare, spider bites can cause pain but are generally considered non-lethal. Australia's infamous Sydney funnel-web spider has never been fatal due to the development of antivenom in 1981. However, always be cautious when handling hairy spiders like tarantulas; they may defend themselves by releasing urticating hairs. These hairs then irritate the attacker's skin or eyes.
